decision.derivedAnswer: E for the symmetric groove shown. C is also possible under the stated tangencies and dimensions.
decision.reason: The 3/8-inch diameter gives radius r = 3/16 inch. The center is 2r from the 60-degree vertex along the angle bisector. If the bisector tilts by θ from vertical, the gap above the shoulder is x = (3/8) cos θ − 5/16 inches. A vertical bisector gives 1/16 inch (E). Taking cos θ = 11/12 gives 1/32 inch (C). The two contact points stay below the shoulder since their distances from the vertex are √3 r < 1/2 inch. Both constructions meet all three tangency conditions. The diagram shows a symmetric groove, but no alignment or symmetry marking requires that configuration. Retain historical key E and accept the ambiguity when grading.
